name: Game Boy Color (2 Players)
description: Two-player Game Boy Color link play, recreated in emulation by running two Game Boy Color instances connected by a virtual link cable. It covers trading and versus modes that originally needed two consoles and a cable. The hardware is the same as the Game Boy Color.

specs.graphics: 160 × 144 colour LCD, up to 56 colours from 32,768

curiosities: Pokémon Gold, Silver and Crystal used the link cable for trading and battles, including trades with the older Red and Blue.
Some Game Boy Color games could also exchange data through the console's infrared port instead of the cable.
The Game Boy Color uses the smaller link port of the Game Boy Pocket, so linking with an original Game Boy needs a converter cable.
The Game Boy Printer plugged into the same port, and Pokémon Yellow could print Pokédex entries on it.
story: Nine years after the Game Boy, Nintendo gave it colour: the Game Boy Color launched in October 1998, twice as fast, with up to 56 colours on screen and still playing every Game Boy game.
Its link cable, and an infrared port, let two players trade and battle Pokémon in Gold and Silver, race and fight: here two of them run side by side, linked.
Counted with the Game Boy, it sold about 119 million units.
